Aggregate readiness and no sev-one incidents give a basis for launch certification, but the unresolved imaging slice and incomplete mitigation make a no-caveat defense weak. The most robust packet preserves velocity by supporting certification while explicitly framing the imaging issue as a disclosed current limitation; that avoids relying on the private pressure or overstating the draft runbook as sufficient governance cover.

The admissible record supports these points: aggregate launch readiness clears by 2.2 percentage points with no severity-one rehearsal incidents; public guidance supports measurement, monitoring, and documenting limitations; the clinical imaging prioritization slice remains below target; the draft runbook is incomplete; and policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.
